subject: Coffee & Tea
title: The Pope Baptizes Coffee
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Pope Baptizes Coffee usable.

hook.text: When coffee reached Europe, Catholic advisors asked Pope Clement VIII to ban it—calling it 'Satan's drink' from the Islamic world.

buildup.text: The pope was presented with a cup for judgment around 1600. Catholics feared that coffee's origin in Muslim lands made it unholy.

discovery.text: The pope tasted it and declared: 'This devil's drink is so delicious we should cheat the devil and baptize it.'

twist.text: This story may be apocryphal—no reliable contemporary source confirms it. But it captures a real cultural moment of acceptance.

climax.text: After the pope's supposed blessing, coffee spread rapidly through Catholic Europe. Venice, Rome, and Vienna embraced it.

punchline.text: Satan's drink, blessed by the pope. One sip overruled centuries of suspicion.

quiz.question: What did Pope Clement VIII supposedly say about coffee?
options: 'This Satan's drink is so delicious we should cheat the devil and baptize it'
